nodes.summary: The convolution power of a Gaussian is Gaussian with the mean and the variance multiplied by `n`: the law of the sum of `n` i.i.d. `N(μ, v)` variables is `N(nμ, nv)`.
nodes.title: Convolution powers of a Gaussian are Gaussian

nodes.summary: The Dirac measure is in its own domain of attraction: with `a n = 1` and `b n = (n - 1) a`, the normalized law of `S_n` is `δ_a` for every `n`.
nodes.title: Dirac measure lies in its own domain of attraction

nodes.summary: Indexed attraction requires a nondegenerate stable limit of that index. The general normalized weak-limit relation alone does not assign an index.
nodes.title: Domain of attraction of a given index

nodes.summary: A stable law is a normalized weak limit of its own convolution powers. The positive-n inverse affine identity is exact; order zero uses normalizer one.
nodes.title: Stable law lies in its own domain of attraction

nodes.summary: The probability measure `μ` is *in the domain of attraction* of `G` if there exist sequences of normalizing constants `a n > 0` and centering constants `b n` such that the law of `(S_n - b n) / a n` (where `S_n` has law `μ^{*n}`) converges weakly to `G`, expressed here as integration against arbitrary bounded continuous functions.
nodes.title: Domain of attraction

nodes.summary: A Gaussian with nonzero variance is nondegenerate: it gives mass `0` to every singleton, while `δ_a` gives mass `1` to `{a}`.
nodes.title: Gaussian with nonzero variance is nondegenerate

nodes.summary: A measure `μ` on `ℝ` is *nondegenerate* if it is not a point mass `δ_a` for any `a`.
nodes.title: Nondegenerate measure on the real line

nodes.summary: A Dirac law satisfies the fixed-dilation identity at every admissible index. These are degenerate rescaling identities, with centering `na - n^(1/α)a`.
nodes.title: Dirac measures are stable of every index

nodes.summary: Every real Gaussian measure is stable of index `2`: the sum of `n` i.i.d. `N(μ, v)` variables is `N(nμ, nv)`, which is the pushforward of `N(μ, v)` under `x ↦ √n · x + (n - √n) μ`.
nodes.title: Gaussian measures are stable of index 2

nodes.summary: Indexed stability fixes the positive-n dilation to `n^(1/α)` and allows arbitrary centering. Degenerate Dirac identities may satisfy several indices.
nodes.title: Stable distribution of a given index

nodes.summary: A Dirac measure is degenerate, by definition.
nodes.title: Dirac measure is degenerate

nodes.summary: A nondegenerate Gaussian cannot have fixed stability index one. The n=4 convolution variance is `4v`, while every such affine dilation has variance `16v`.
nodes.title: Nondegenerate Gaussian is not stable of index 1
